category_title: Eighteen-year-old autistic student acting as an online upstander despite literacy challenges
minimal_context: The student and a staff member are having a one-on-one discussion at school about an online argument the student was involved in.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's discuss what happened online yesterday when you tried to argue with the other students.

STUDENT: He was picking on a little kid. It was the wrong thing to do, so I told him to take the video down.

TUTOR: What did they say to you?

STUDENT: He said it was nothing to do with me, but he was out of order. Then he started abusing me for my poor spelling.

TUTOR: What did you do then?

STUDENT: I started trying to argue my corner! But then five other students joined in and started ganging up on me, ridiculing my spelling. It was five pupils against one girl and I couldn't defend myself!

options.A: Avoid intervening too soon in the one-on-one discussion by allowing wait time for the student to respond.
options.B: Ask a follow-up question that links physical sensations to a potential emotional state during the one-on-one discussion.
options.C: Speak to the involved individuals at school and have the deputy head undertake a cyberbullying education session in assembly.
options.D: Ask closed-end questions about the online argument during the remainder of the one-on-one discussion.
